name: Today's Report
headline: Consumer mood is near a record low, and buyers point to the same two things home shoppers feel: high prices and borrowing costs.
teaser: Consumers are in a sour mood. The University of Michigan's sentiment index slipped to a preliminary 46.3 in October from 48.1. If it holds, that is the second lowest reading since the survey began in 1952, behind only May's 44.8. Before this year, the low was 50.0 in June 2022.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Consumers are in a sour mood. The University of Michigan's sentiment index slipped to a preliminary 46.3 in October from 48.1. If it holds, that is the second lowest reading since the survey began in 1952, behind only May's 44.8. Before this year, the low was 50.0 in June 2022.

The survey's director said buying conditions for big ticket items "plummeted amid high prices and borrowing costs," and year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.7% from 4.6%. Home buyers know the feeling: Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fixed is 7.48% and the 15-year 7.15%. Those are Friday's readings, since the bond market is closed for Columbus Day.

Locally, a cautious buyer shows up as patience. Across our five cities, 156 of the 611 homes on the market have been listed 60 days or longer, up from 148 on Sunday. The five city ledger reads 686, up from 684. Fremont rose to 241 and Milpitas to 101, Newark slipped to 90, and Hayward (192) and Union City (62) held. The board wide table eased to 2,661 from 2,662.

What this means for you: a gloomy survey is not a market crash, but it does thin the crowd. Buyers who are ready can find sellers more willing to talk, especially on homes that have sat 60 days or more. Sellers should price for the buyer who is actually showing up, not the one from last spring.

  • Board wide: 2,661 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 158 coming soon and 222 brand new.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Live ledger: 686 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 611 are on the market and 75 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 241 live, 197 active, 28 coming soon and 16 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,275,000 at $797 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 34 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 192, Milpitas 101, Newark 90, Union City 62.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,075,000 at $676 a square foot. 287 homes are priced under a million, and 156 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

images.alt: Line chart of the University of Michigan index of consumer sentiment in 2026: 56.4 in January, 56.6 in February, 53.3 in March, 49.8 in April, a record low of 44.8 in May, 49.5 in June, 55.2 in July, 51.7 in August, 48.1 in September and a preliminary 46.3 in October. A dashed line marks 50.0, the lowest reading before 2026, set in June 2022.
images.caption: October's preliminary 46.3 would be the second lowest reading on record, behind May's 44.8. Before 2026, the low was 50.0.
images.source: Source: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers; October is preliminary (released Oct. 9, 2026), and the final is due Oct. 23.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
France now pays more to borrow than Italy. France's 10-year yield closed Friday at 4.86% against Italy's 4.60%, per CNBC data. Thursday's gap of 0.28 points was the widest in data back to 1999. At the start of 2024, Italy paid 1.12 points more than France.

France first edged above Italy in October 2025 and has stayed above since early August. Its 10-year is now the highest since 2002, and its gap over Germany (3.49%) is 1.37 points. Spain pays 4.11%. The bond market, it seems, has stopped grading on reputation.

For American borrowers the takeaway is that rates are high everywhere. The U.S. 10-Year closed Friday at 5.24%, above all four, and that is the yield mortgage rates follow.

images.alt: Bar chart of 10-year government bond yields at Friday's close, Oct. 9, 2026: France 4.86%, Italy 4.60%, Spain 4.11%, Germany 3.49%, with the U.S. 10-Year Treasury at 5.24% for comparison. A second panel shows France's yield minus Italy's since January 2024, rising from about minus 1.1 points to above zero for the first time on Oct. 7, 2025, and to plus 0.26 points on Oct. 9, 2026.
images.caption: France's 10-year yield closed Friday 0.26 points above Italy's. At the start of 2024, Italy paid 1.12 points more.
images.source: Source: CNBC daily closing yields, Jan. 1999 to Oct. 9, 2026; U.S. Treasury daily yield curve.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Stocks are trading on Columbus Day even though the bond market is closed. Late Monday morning the S&P 500 and the Dow are higher while the Nasdaq is lower, after all three finished last week higher. The S&P 500 is up 14.1% this year.

Earnings season starts Tuesday, when JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and Citigroup report, along with Johnson & Johnson. Banks are a good read on whether that sour consumer mood is showing up in actual spending and borrowing.
